thread:
incident-bot: PAGING: Latency SLO breach (hosted-api us-east-1) — p95 bound crossed, p99 elevated. Auto-posting to #incidents and paging oncall.

Hannah T.: seeing a spike in streaming tail latencies. p95 from ~300ms -> 900ms, p99 up to 6s. Affected tenants: high-throughput ones mostly. Dash: https://metrics.redwood/edge/us-east-1/latency

Ibrahim N.: looks correlated with a jump in control-plane calls per request. Each stream is making multiple config/flag checks per segment. Count of config-fetch calls per stream up ~4x since 2025-04-02T14:22Z.

Jules P.: deploy-bot: no application deploys in the last hour. infra deploy to control-plane at 2025-04-02T13:05Z (older).

Kara M.: Logs show repeated 429s and tcp timeouts from config-service behind the control-plane gateway. Snippet: 
```
WARN config-client: request failed status=429 retry=1 tenant=acct-121
ERROR gateway: upstream conn reset config-service id=svc-config-1
```

Liam Ops: Checking DB metrics — auth_db connections spiking, rate_limit_db shows burst of writes, and featureflags cache hit ratio dropped to 22%. I suspect cache eviction storm.

Maya S.: Correlating with a scheduled job? We had a cron at 14:20 that invalidates caches for rollout verification. Could be causing cache-thundering. I'm pulling the cron logs now.

incident-bot: automation: cronjob/ff-verifier ran at 2025-04-02T14:20:15Z — duration 03:12.

Hannah T.: Customer impact: multiple streaming clients see partial streams (good chunks then long pause). UX: spinner then reconnection. No data loss but elevated tail latency causes timeouts on some client SDKs. Currently about 4% of streaming requests impacted.

Ibrahim N.: Mitigation idea 1: pause the ff-verifier cron to stop cache invalidation storm. Mitigation 2: add short-circuit in streaming path to use last-known config if config fetch >150ms. Mitigation 3: temporarily raise rate limits for control-plane internal calls.

Jules P.: I'm pausing the cron now. kubectl patch cronjob/ff-verifier -n controlplane --patch '{"spec": {"suspend": true}}'

Kara M.: Paused. Monitoring cache hit ratio. Also scaling config-service pods + autoscaler min from 3 -> 6 to absorb burst. kubectl scale deployment/config-service --replicas=6 -n controlplane

Liam Ops: Increasing internal rate limit for control-plane calls by factor 2 to prevent 429s. Pushing change to gateway config: gateway.rate_limits.controlplane=200rps -> 400rps (temp).

Maya S.: Enabling short-circuit fallback in streaming client to skip feature-flag evaluation for non-critical flags. Rolling to 15% of streaming nodes. Patch: featureflags.client.fallback_on_error=true; rollout=15%

Hannah T.: After cron pause and scaling, config-service 5xx/429 dropped significantly. Cache hit ratio climbing back to ~68%. p95 improves to ~360ms, p99 ~1.2s. Still watching tail anomalies.

Ibrahim N.: There are a few tenants still observing replays — digging deeper on token churn. Token service logs show token-issuing rate spike; token cache TTL looks low for certain edge nodes (60s). Suggest bumping token cache TTL to 300s for edge frontends.

Jules P.: Bumping in progress: infra-ops applied env var change AUTH_TOKEN_TTL=300 on edge pool (rolling restart).

Kara M.: Also discovered a schema migration from last week removed an index unintentionally on feature_flag_segments. Putting in place a concurrent index creation now to help select times. CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_seg_org_flag ON feature_flag_segments (org_id, flag_id);

Liam Ops: Pre-warming DB connections and increasing pool size on control-plane from 150 -> 350 to reduce waiters. Doing this as a short-term emergency config change.

Maya S.: Monitoring shows dropped error rate and latencies trending down. p95 ~280ms, p99 ~850ms. Client-side timeouts still firing for older SDK versions; flagging client-upgrade note to SDK team.

incident-bot: UPDATE: mitigations applied. auto-page cleared. Continue to monitor for 45m.

Hannah T.: On-call handoff: handing to Ibrahim N. at 15:10Z for the stabilization window. I'll add timeline and actions to the incident ticket.

Ibrahim N.: Handoff ack. Next steps: (1) ensure index completes (watch pg_locks), (2) keep cron suspended until root cause confirmed, (3) roll out fallback to 50% if any re-regress, (4) coordinate post-incident comms.

Jules P.: Post-incident customer notes prepared and queued for status.redwood.com. Suggest mentioning temporary degraded streaming UX and actions taken.

Kara M.: RCA owner assigned: Kara M. to investigate cache invalidation logic in ff-verifier and how it triggers eviction across shared caches. Dibs on migration audit.

Maya S.: I'll open a PR for streaming degraded-mode: handshake continues with last-known config and emits an event to clients indicating flags are stale. PR link: https://git.redwood/pr/4672

incident-bot: RESOLVE: incident marked mitigated at 2025-04-02T15:27Z. Please produce postmortem within 72h.

Liam Ops: Adding final runbook notes: if cache invalidation job > 1min or >10% of caches affected, suspend job and scale config-service first.

Ibrahim N.: Thanks team — leaving notes for postmortem. Will escalate if any regression in next 2h. :thumbsup:
notes: oncall-handoff: Hannah T. -> Ibrahim N.; rca-owner: Kara M.; mitigations: cron_pause_ff_verifier, config-service_scale, gateway_rate_limit_bump, token_cache_ttl_bump, featureflag_fallback_rollout, index_concurrent_create, db_pool_increase
